Class StatsPanel

java.lang.Object
javafx.scene.Node
javafx.scene.Parent
javafx.scene.layout.Region
javafx.scene.layout.Pane
javafx.scene.layout.StackPane
it.polimi.ingsw.client.ui.gui.StatsPanel
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.css.Styleable, javafx.event.EventTarget
public class StatsPanel extends javafx.scene.layout.StackPane
Collapsible side panel displaying the opponent players' statistics during a game session.

Rendered as a slide-in drawer anchored to the top-right corner of the game board (managed by GameController). The panel consists of:

  • A vertical tab label (toggleLabel) rotated 90° that acts as the click target to expand or collapse the drawer.
  • A VBox (opponents) populated at runtime by GameController with one entry per opponent, typically showing food, stars, prestige points and hand size.

The drawer is collapsed synchronously at construction time (see collapseImmediately()), translated off-screen to the right by the width of opponents so only the tab remains visible. Clicking the tab triggers a 250 ms TranslateTransition that slides the full panel into view or hides it again.

The panel uses pickOnBounds = false so that the transparent area outside the drawer does not intercept mouse events on the board beneath it.

    • opponents

      private final javafx.scene.layout.VBox opponents
      Container populated at runtime with one stats row per opponent. Accessible externally via getOpponents() so that GameController can add and update its children.

    • drawer

      private final javafx.scene.layout.HBox drawer
      Horizontal container holding the toggleLabel tab and the opponents pane side by side. Slide animation is applied to this node via translateX.

      Rotated label acting as the clickable toggle tab on the right edge of the screen. Its text reflects the current expanded/collapsed state.

  • Constructor Details

    • StatsPanel

      public StatsPanel()
      Constructs a StatsPanel with an empty opponents list and a collapsed drawer.

      The drawer's initial off-screen translation is deferred until the first layout pass via a width listener, since the node's dimensions are not available at construction time.

  • Method Details

    • collapseImmediately

      private void collapseImmediately()
      Forces a synchronous CSS + layout pass on drawer and immediately applies the collapsed translation, so the panel never renders in its expanded position even for a single frame.

      This replaces a reactive widthProperty listener approach: waiting for a layout-triggered property change is timing-dependent on when the panel is attached to the scene and shown, which could let an expanded frame slip through before the listener fires. drawer does not need to be attached to a Scene for this: it already has tabGroup and opponents as children, which is enough for JavaFX to compute its preferred size in isolation.

    • snapCollapsed

      public void snapCollapsed()
      Re-applies the collapsed position using the drawer's current content width.

      collapseImmediately() runs at construction time, when opponents is still empty, so the resulting offset is based on a near-zero width. GameController populates opponents with one row per opponent shortly after construction; without a re-snap the drawer is wider than the stale offset accounts for, so the panel appears expanded at the start of a match even though expanded is false. Calling this once after the initial population corrects the offset. No-op if the drawer is currently expanded.

      Must be called on the FX Application Thread.

    • getOpponents

      public javafx.scene.layout.VBox getOpponents()
      Returns the VBox that holds the opponent stats rows.

      Called by GameController to add, update, or remove per-opponent stat entries as the game state changes.

      Returns:
      the opponents container VBox

    • toggleDrawer

      private void toggleDrawer()
      Toggles the drawer between its expanded and collapsed states, animating the transition with a 250 ms TranslateTransition.

      When expanding, the drawer slides left until fully visible (translateX = 0). When collapsing, it slides right until only the tab label remains on screen (translateX = opponents.getWidth()). The toggle label arrow is updated to reflect the new state.
